{{Short description|1929 academic paper by Ludwig Wittgenstein}}
"'''Some Remarks on Logical Form'''" (1929<ref>{{cite journal |first=Ludwig |last=Wittgenstein |title=Some Remarks on Logical Form |journal=[[Aristotelian Society|Proc. Aristot. Soc. Suppl. Vol.]] |volume=9 |issue=1 |date=15 July 1929 |page=162–171 |url=https://wittgensteinproject.org/w/index.php/Some_Remarks_on_Logical_Form |doi=10.1093/aristoteliansupp/9.1.162 |doi-access=free }}</ref>) was the only academic paper ever published by [[Ludwig Wittgenstein]]. It contained Wittgenstein's thinking on [[logic]] and the [[Wittgenstein's philosophy of mathematics|philosophy of mathematics]] immediately before the rupture that divided the [[early Wittgenstein]] of the ''[[Tractatus Logico-Philosophicus]]'' from the [[later Wittgenstein]] represented in the ''[[Philosophical Investigations]]''.<ref name=:0>{{cite journal | doi=10.1007/BF00485322 | volume=56 | issue=2 | title=Some remarks on (Wittgensteinian) logical form | year=1983 | journal=[[Synthese]] | pages=155–170 | last1 = Hintikka | first1 = Jaakko | last2 = Hintikka | first2 = Merrill B.}}</ref> The approach to [[logical form]] in the paper reflected [[Frank P. Ramsey]]'s critique of Wittgenstein's account of color in the ''Tractatus'', and has been analyzed by [[G. E. M. Anscombe]] and [[Jaakko Hintikka]], among others.<ref name=:0/> In a [[letter to the editor]] of [[Mind (journal)|''Mind'']] in 1933 Wittgenstein referred to it as "a short (and weak) article".<ref>{{cite book |title=Wittgenstein in Cambridge Letters and Documents 1911 - 1951 |date=2012 |publisher=Wiley |page=210}}</ref>
